h-uruk-period.summary: Uruk grows into one of the first large cities. Its period gives its name to the age.

h-cuneiform.summary: Scribes in southern Mesopotamia turn accounting marks into cuneiform. It is the earliest known writing system.

h-ziggurat-of-ur.summary: King Ur-Nammu raises a stepped temple tower for the moon god at Ur.

h-akkadian-empire.summary: Sargon of Akkad unites the city-states of southern Mesopotamia. Many call it the first empire.

h-gilgamesh.summary: Scribes join older Sumerian poems into one Akkadian epic. It is the oldest surviving narrative literature.

h-code-of-hammurabi.summary: Hammurabi of Babylon has a code of laws carved on a tall stone stele.

h-battle-of-kadesh.summary: Ramesses II of Egypt meets the Hittite army of Muwatalli II on the Orontes River.

h-bronze-age-collapse.summary: Kingdoms across the eastern Mediterranean fall or shrink. Cities such as Ugarit are destroyed.

h-narmer.summary: Many scholars see Narmer as the first king of a unified Egypt. He founds the First Dynasty.

h-pyramid-of-djoser.summary: Egypt builds its first pyramid as a tomb for King Djoser.

h-great-pyramid.summary: Workers build the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu over about 26 years. It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders.

h-kerma.summary: A Nubian kingdom grows at Kerma on the Nile. At its height it rivals Egypt.

h-hyksos.summary: Kings of foreign origin rule Lower and Middle Egypt from Avaris in the Nile Delta.

h-nok.summary: A farming culture in central Nigeria later makes the region's earliest known terracotta sculptures.

h-bantu-expansion.summary: Bantu-speaking farmers begin a slow spread across central and southern Africa. It lasts for thousands of years.

h-amarna.summary: Akhenaten builds a new capital and puts the sun disc Aten above the other gods.

h-tutankhamun.summary: The boy king restores Egypt's traditional gods after Akhenaten. He dies at about 19.

h-newgrange.summary: Farmers in Ireland build a great passage tomb above the River Boyne. It is older than the pyramids.

h-otzi.summary: A man dies high in the Alps, and the ice preserves his body. It is Europe's oldest known natural mummy.

h-stonehenge.summary: People dig the first ditch and bank on Salisbury Plain. The stones are set up in later centuries.

h-knossos.summary: The Minoans of Crete build a palace at Knossos. It becomes their largest center.

h-thera-eruption.summary: A huge volcanic eruption destroys Akrotiri on Thera. Its exact date is still debated.

h-mycenae.summary: The Mycenaean Greeks extend the great walls of their citadel at Mycenae.

h-sintashta.summary: People of the southern Urals build fortified settlements. Many scholars link them to the earliest Indo-Iranian languages.

h-indus-valley.summary: Planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro flourish along the Indus. The civilisation covers more land than Egypt and Mesopotamia combined.

h-rigveda.summary: Poets in the northwest of India compose Sanskrit hymns. They become the oldest of the four Vedas.

h-liangzhu.summary: A jade-working society builds a large center near modern Hangzhou. It may be one of East Asia's first states.

h-sannai-maruyama.summary: Jōmon people in northern Japan settle a village with hundreds of pit houses.

h-erlitou.summary: A Bronze Age society grows in the Yellow River valley. Many archaeologists see it as China's first state.

h-shang-dynasty.summary: Shang kings rule from capitals such as Yin. Their oracle bones hold the earliest known Chinese writing.

h-battle-of-muye.summary: King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king. The Zhou dynasty begins.

h-caral.summary: Communities on the coast of Peru build large plazas and mounds. It is the oldest known civilization in the Americas.

h-valdivia.summary: Villagers on the Ecuador coast make some of the earliest pottery in the Americas.

h-poverty-point.summary: People in the lower Mississippi valley build great earthen ridges and mounds.

h-paso-de-la-amada.summary: Villagers on the Pacific coast of Chiapas build a court for the Mesoamerican ballgame.

h-olmec-san-lorenzo.summary: The Olmec make San Lorenzo their main center. They carve colossal stone heads.

h-austronesian-expansion.summary: Seafarers from Taiwan begin settling the islands of Southeast Asia. Their descendants later reach the Pacific and Madagascar.

h-lapita.summary: Austronesian seafarers with stamped pottery settle Island Melanesia. They are ancestors of the Polynesians.

h-ashurbanipal-library.summary: The Assyrian king collects clay tablets on every subject. More than 30,000 tablets and fragments survive.

h-fall-of-nineveh.summary: An alliance of Babylonians and Medes sacks the Assyrian capital. The Assyrian Empire soon collapses.

h-achaemenid-empire.summary: Cyrus of Persia founds the Achaemenid Empire. Its kings come to rule from Egypt to the Indus.

h-persepolis.summary: Persian kings begin a great ceremonial capital. Alexander's army burns its palaces in 330 BCE.

h-alexander-invades-persia.summary: Alexander of Macedon crosses into Asia and conquers the Persian Empire. He dies at Babylon in 323 BCE.

h-seleucid-empire.summary: One of Alexander's generals takes the eastern part of his empire. His dynasty rules from Mesopotamia to Syria.

h-parthian-empire.summary: The Arsacid dynasty founds an Iranian empire. It later becomes Rome's great rival in the east.

h-olympic-games.summary: Greek tradition dates the first games at Olympia to this year.

h-founding-of-rome.summary: Roman tradition sets the city's founding in this year. Archaeology shows earlier villages on its hills.

h-athenian-democracy.summary: Cleisthenes gives power to an assembly of citizens. Athenian democracy grows from these reforms.

h-battle-of-marathon.summary: Athenian soldiers defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece.

h-parthenon.summary: Athens builds a temple to Athena on the Acropolis. It thanks the goddess for victory over Persia.

h-la-tene.summary: A Celtic Iron Age culture spreads across much of Europe. It lasts until the Roman conquest.

h-hannibal-alps.summary: The Carthaginian general leads his army and elephants over the Alps into Italy.

h-caesar-assassinated.summary: Senators kill the Roman dictator during a Senate session. Civil war follows.

h-augustus.summary: Octavian takes the name Augustus and rules as emperor. The Roman Republic gives way to the Empire.

h-scythians.summary: Mounted Scythian nomads become the dominant power on the western Eurasian steppe.

h-carthage.summary: Merchants from Tyre found Carthage in North Africa. It grows into a great sea power.

h-kushite-pharaohs.summary: Kings from Kush in Nubia rule Egypt as its Twenty-fifth Dynasty for nearly a century.

h-meroe.summary: The Kingdom of Kush rules from Meroë on the Nile for centuries.

h-library-of-alexandria.summary: Scholars gather at the great library of Ptolemaic Egypt. They study Homer, mathematics, and the stars.

h-djenne-djenno.summary: People settle a site in the inland Niger delta. It becomes one of West Africa's oldest towns.

h-the-buddha.summary: A wandering teacher in the Ganges plain founds Buddhism. Scholars debate the exact years of his life.

h-maurya-empire.summary: Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire across northern India. It is one of the largest in Indian history.

h-edicts-of-ashoka.summary: The Maurya emperor Ashoka has moral teachings carved on pillars and rocks across India.

h-eastern-zhou.summary: The Eastern Zhou period begins. Local lords gain power as royal power weakens.

h-confucius.summary: The philosopher Kong Qiu teaches ethics and good government. His ideas shape China for millennia.

h-qin-unification.summary: The state of Qin conquers its rivals. Its king becomes the first emperor of China.

h-terracotta-army.summary: Thousands of clay soldiers are buried with the first emperor to guard him after death.

h-han-dynasty.summary: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty after the fall of Qin. Han rule lasts about four centuries.

h-xiongnu.summary: Nomads of the eastern steppe unite under one leader. They become a great rival of Han China.

h-silk-road.summary: A Han envoy's journeys to Central Asia open trade routes to the west.

h-yayoi.summary: Rice farming and metalwork spread across the Japanese islands. Some scholars date the start earlier.

h-la-venta.summary: After San Lorenzo declines, La Venta becomes the main Olmec city. Its people carve colossal heads.

h-chavin.summary: A religious center in the Peruvian Andes draws pilgrims from a wide region.

h-paracas.summary: An Andean society in southern Peru weaves some of the finest ancient textiles.

h-el-mirador.summary: The Maya build huge temples at El Mirador in the Petén. It peaks from the 3rd century BCE.

h-monte-alban.summary: The Zapotec build a hilltop city in the Oaxaca valley. It becomes their capital.

h-adena.summary: Woodland peoples in the Ohio valley build burial mounds and earthworks.

h-tonga-settled.summary: Seafarers of the Lapita culture reach Tonga. It is the first island settled in Polynesia.

h-siege-of-jerusalem-70.summary: Roman legions take Jerusalem during the First Jewish Revolt. The temple is destroyed and never rebuilt.

h-sasanian-empire.summary: Ardashir defeats the last Parthian king. His Sasanian dynasty rules Iran until 651.

h-council-of-nicaea.summary: Bishops from across the Roman Empire meet at Nicaea. They issue the first form of the Nicene Creed.

h-hijrah.summary: Muhammad leaves Mecca for Medina. The year becomes the start of the Islamic calendar.

h-dome-of-the-rock.summary: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik builds a shrine over the rock on the Temple Mount.

h-round-city-baghdad.summary: Caliph al-Mansur builds a round city on the Tigris. It becomes the Abbasid capital.

h-vesuvius-79.summary: Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.

h-trajan.summary: By the death of Emperor Trajan, Roman rule stretches farther than ever before.

h-edict-of-milan.summary: Constantine and Licinius agree to tolerate Christians across the Roman Empire.

h-constantinople.summary: Constantine makes the old city of Byzantium his new capital. It stays a capital for 1,100 years.

h-fall-of-western-rome.summary: Odoacer removes Romulus Augustulus. Many historians date the end of the Western Roman Empire here.

h-hagia-sophia.summary: The emperor Justinian completes a great domed church. It becomes the largest interior space in the world.

h-lindisfarne.summary: Norse raiders sack the abbey on Lindisfarne. Many date the start of the Viking Age here.

h-charlemagne.summary: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king as emperor in Rome.

h-aksum-christianity.summary: Under King Ezana the Ethiopian kingdom of Aksum makes Christianity its state religion.

h-arab-conquest-egypt.summary: The Rashidun Caliphate takes Egypt from the Eastern Roman Empire.

h-igbo-ukwu.summary: Igbo-Ukwu becomes the capital of the Kingdom of Nri. Its artisans cast detailed bronzes.

h-ghana-empire.summary: The scholar al-Khwārizmī first names the West African empire of Ghana. It grows rich on Saharan trade.

h-kushan-empire.summary: The Yuezhi found an empire linking Central Asia and northern India along the Silk Road.

h-gupta-empire.summary: The Guptas rule much of northern India. Science, art, and literature flourish.

h-nalanda.summary: A Gupta emperor founds a great Buddhist center of learning. It draws students from across Asia.

h-ajanta.summary: Monks and patrons carve and paint Buddhist caves in western India. Older accounts date this phase earlier.

h-chola-rise.summary: The Chola dynasty of southern India begins its imperial age.

h-cai-lun-paper.summary: A Han court official makes paper from bark, hemp, rags, and fishnets. Paper soon replaces bamboo slips.

h-sui-dynasty.summary: The short Sui dynasty unites China after centuries of division.

h-tang-dynasty.summary: The Tang dynasty rules China for nearly three centuries. Trade and the arts flourish.

h-silla-unification.summary: Allied with Tang China, the kingdom of Silla conquers its rivals Paekche and Goguryeo.

h-nara.summary: Japan builds its first permanent imperial capital at Heijō-kyō, now Nara.

h-diamond-sutra.summary: A woodblock copy of a Buddhist text is printed in Tang China. It is often called the oldest surviving printed book.

h-srivijaya.summary: A Chinese monk studies at Srivijaya on Sumatra. The kingdom is a center of Buddhism and sea trade.

h-borobudur.summary: Builders in central Java raise a vast Buddhist monument in stone terraces.

h-khmer-empire.summary: Jayavarman II declares himself universal king. The Khmer Empire grows to rule much of mainland Southeast Asia.

h-gokturks.summary: The Göktürks overthrow the Rouran and found a steppe empire across Central Asia.

h-battle-of-talas.summary: Abbasid and Tibetan forces defeat a Tang army in Central Asia.

h-teotihuacan.summary: A planned city with great pyramids grows in the Valley of Mexico. At its height it is the largest in the Americas.

h-moche.summary: The Moche build adobe pyramids and make fine pottery on Peru's north coast.

h-tiwanaku.summary: A highland city near Lake Titicaca leads the southern Andes.

h-pakal.summary: The Maya king Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal rebuilds Palenque. His tomb lies in the Temple of the Inscriptions.

h-maya-collapse.summary: Tikal, Palenque, Copán, and Calakmul decline and are abandoned. The causes are still debated.

h-chaco-canyon.summary: Ancestral Puebloans build great houses of stone in the American Southwest.

h-great-schism.summary: The Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches break communion. Scholars debate whether 1054 is the true turning point.

h-norman-conquest.summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold Godwinson at Hastings and takes the English crown.

h-university-of-bologna.summary: Students in Bologna organize to hire teachers of law. It grows into Europe's oldest university.

h-magna-carta.summary: Rebel barons force the English king to accept limits on royal power.

h-hundred-years-war.summary: England and France fight a long series of wars over the French throne.

h-black-death.summary: A plague pandemic sweeps across Europe and kills a large part of its people.

h-gutenberg.summary: Johannes Gutenberg develops printing with movable metal type. His press later prints the Gutenberg Bible.

h-fall-of-constantinople.summary: The Ottoman army takes Constantinople after a 53-day siege. The Byzantine Empire ends.

h-granada-1492.summary: The last Muslim kingdom in Iberia surrenders to Castile. Jews are expelled from Spain the same year.

h-first-crusade-jerusalem.summary: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem after a siege. The crusaders found the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

h-saladin-jerusalem.summary: The Ayyubid sultan Saladin takes Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin. The Third Crusade follows.

h-sack-of-baghdad.summary: Hulegu's Mongol army takes Baghdad and ends the Abbasid Caliphate there.

h-ain-jalut.summary: The Mamluks of Egypt defeat a Mongol army in Galilee. The Mongol advance west is halted.

h-ottoman-empire.summary: A Turkoman leader founds a small state in Anatolia. It grows into the Ottoman Empire.

h-tale-of-genji.summary: Murasaki Shikibu writes a long tale of the Japanese court. It is a classic of world literature.

h-bi-sheng.summary: A Song dynasty artisan prints with fired clay pieces, one for each character.

h-kamakura.summary: Warrior families rule Japan through a military government at Kamakura.

h-mongol-empire.summary: A council proclaims Temüjin ruler of all Mongols. His empire becomes the largest contiguous land empire.

h-yuan-dynasty.summary: The Mongol ruler Kublai Khan governs China as emperor of a new dynasty.

h-ming-dynasty.summary: The Ming drive out the Mongol Yuan rulers. Ming emperors rule China for nearly three centuries.

h-zheng-he.summary: A Ming admiral leads seven great fleets across the Indian Ocean. They reach Arabia and East Africa.

h-forbidden-city.summary: The Ming build a vast palace complex in Beijing. It remains the imperial seat until 1924.

h-timur.summary: The conqueror Timur rules Central Asia and Iran from Samarkand.

h-brihadisvara.summary: The Chola emperor Rajaraja I builds a towering temple to Shiva.

h-delhi-sultanate.summary: Turkic rulers found a sultanate at Delhi. Its dynasties rule much of northern India for three centuries.

h-vijayanagara.summary: Two brothers found a south Indian empire with its capital at Vijayanagara, now Hampi.

h-angkor-wat.summary: The Khmer king Suryavarman II builds a vast temple at his capital.

h-majapahit.summary: Raden Wijaya founds a Javanese empire after a Mongol invasion. It comes to rule much of the archipelago.

h-ayutthaya.summary: A Thai kingdom rises at Ayutthaya. It lasts for more than four centuries.

h-great-zimbabwe.summary: Shona builders raise great stone walls in southern Africa. The city becomes a royal capital.

h-lalibela.summary: Churches are carved down into solid rock in the Ethiopian highlands. Tradition credits King Lalibela.

h-mansa-musa.summary: The ruler of Mali travels to Mecca with a vast entourage and much gold. Mali is at its height.

h-kilwa.summary: A Swahili trading city on the East African coast builds a great palace.

h-kongo.summary: A marriage alliance joins two peoples into the Kingdom of Kongo in central Africa.

h-songhai.summary: Sonni Ali of Songhai takes the great trading cities of the Niger.

h-lanse-aux-meadows.summary: Norse voyagers build a small settlement in North America. It is the only undisputed Norse site there.

h-cahokia.summary: The Mississippian city by the Mississippi River has about 120 earthworks at its peak.

h-inca-rise.summary: The Inca state grows from the highlands around Cusco. It later becomes the largest empire in the Americas.

h-tenochtitlan.summary: The Mexica build their city on an island in Lake Texcoco. It becomes the Aztec capital.

h-chan-chan.summary: The Chimú rule the north coast of Peru from a vast adobe city. The Inca conquer them around 1470.

h-columbus-1492.summary: Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas for Spain. Lasting contact between Europe and the Americas begins.

h-hawaii-settled.summary: Polynesian voyagers reach the Hawaiian Islands and settle them.

h-rapa-nui-settled.summary: Voyagers reach one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth. Its people later carve the moai statues.

h-aotearoa-settled.summary: East Polynesian voyagers settle New Zealand. Their descendants become the Māori.

h-ninety-five-theses.summary: Martin Luther challenges the sale of indulgences. The Protestant Reformation grows from the dispute.

h-magellan-expedition.summary: A Spanish fleet sails west under Magellan. After his death, Elcano brings one ship home around the world.

h-copernicus.summary: Nicolaus Copernicus places the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the universe.

h-spanish-armada.summary: A great Spanish fleet sails to invade England and fails.

h-king-james-bible.summary: The Church of England publishes a new English translation of the Bible. It is read widely for centuries.

h-thirty-years-war.summary: Religious and political conflict tears through Central Europe. It is one of Europe's most destructive wars.

h-galileo-dialogue.summary: Galileo defends a Sun-centered universe in print. The Inquisition later puts him on trial.

h-peace-of-westphalia.summary: Two treaties end the Thirty Years' War. They shape the European system of states.

h-battle-of-vienna.summary: A relief army breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna. Ottoman expansion into Europe begins to reverse.

h-newton-principia.summary: Isaac Newton sets out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

h-saint-petersburg.summary: The tsar builds a new city on the Baltic. It becomes the capital of the Russian Empire.

h-storming-of-the-bastille.summary: Crowds in Paris seize a royal fortress. It becomes the symbol of the French Revolution.

h-safavid-iran.summary: The Safavids found a new Iranian empire and make Shia Islam its state religion.

h-suleiman.summary: The Ottoman Empire reaches its height under Suleiman. His armies besiege Vienna in 1529.

h-atlantic-slave-trade.summary: European traders ship about 12.75 million Africans to the Americas as slaves. Up to 2 million die on the voyage.

h-tondibi.summary: A Moroccan army with firearms defeats the Songhai Empire near Gao.

h-nzinga.summary: Nzinga leads the Ambundu kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba against Portuguese conquest.

h-gondar.summary: Emperor Fasilides settles his court at Gondar and builds a stone castle.

h-cape-colony.summary: The Dutch East India Company builds a supply post at the Cape of Good Hope. A colony grows from it.

h-asante-empire.summary: Osei Tutu unites the Asante under the Golden Stool. The empire lasts two centuries.

h-panipat-1526.summary: Babur defeats the Sultan of Delhi at Panipat. His Mughal dynasty comes to rule most of India.

h-taj-mahal.summary: Shah Jahan builds a white marble tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

h-plassey.summary: The British East India Company defeats the Nawab of Bengal. British rule in India begins to grow.

h-macau.summary: Portuguese traders found a settlement on the south China coast. It stays Portuguese until 1999.

h-imjin-war.summary: Japanese armies invade Korea twice. Korea and Ming China drive them out.

h-sekigahara.summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins control of Japan in a great battle.

h-tokugawa-shogunate.summary: The Tokugawa shoguns rule Japan from Edo for more than two and a half centuries.

h-qing-beijing.summary: The Manchu Qing dynasty takes the Ming capital. It rules China until 1912.

h-malacca-1511.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque takes the great trading port on the Strait of Malacca.

h-manila-1571.summary: Miguel López de Legazpi makes Manila the capital of the Spanish Philippines. Its galleons link Asia and the Americas.

h-batavia.summary: The Dutch East India Company builds its Asian headquarters on Java.

h-dzungars.summary: Western Mongol peoples unite in Dzungaria. They later build the Dzungar Khanate.

h-fall-of-tenochtitlan.summary: Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies take the Aztec capital. Spanish rule of Mexico begins.

h-cajamarca.summary: Spanish soldiers seize the last Sapa Inca at Cajamarca. The conquest of the Inca Empire begins.

h-potosi.summary: Silver from a mountain in the Andes makes Potosí rich. It becomes a major city of the Spanish Empire.

h-jamestown.summary: The Virginia Company founds the first lasting English settlement in North America.

h-plymouth-colony.summary: English separatists from the Mayflower found the first permanent colony in New England.

h-declaration-of-independence.summary: Thirteen American colonies declare independence from Great Britain.

h-us-constitution.summary: Delegates in Philadelphia draft a new framework of government for the United States.

h-haitian-revolution.summary: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise against French rule. They found the free nation of Haiti.

h-tasman-1642.summary: A Dutch voyage reaches Tasmania and New Zealand. It is the first known European visit to either.

h-cook-first-voyage.summary: Cook observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti. He then charts New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.

h-first-fleet.summary: British ships carrying convicts found a penal colony at Port Jackson. Colonization of Australia begins.

h-slave-trade-act-1807.summary: Parliament prohibits the Atlantic slave trade across the British Empire.

h-waterloo.summary: A coalition army defeats Napoleon in Belgium. His rule of France ends.

h-origin-of-species.summary: Charles Darwin sets out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

h-german-empire.summary: The German states unite under Prussia. The new empire is proclaimed at Versailles.

h-world-war-i.summary: An assassination in Sarajevo sets off a global war between two great alliances. Millions die.

h-russian-revolution.summary: Revolution ends the Russian monarchy. The Bolsheviks seize power later that year.

h-world-war-ii.summary: Germany's invasion of Poland begins a world war between the Allies and the Axis. It is the deadliest war in history.

h-world-wide-web.summary: Tim Berners-Lee invents the Web at CERN. It opens to the public in 1993.

h-berlin-wall.summary: East Germany opens the border in Berlin. The division of Europe begins to end.

h-soviet-dissolution.summary: The Soviet Union ceases to exist. Fifteen republics become independent states.

h-ottoman-sultanate-abolished.summary: Turkey's Grand National Assembly abolishes the sultanate. The Republic of Turkey follows.

h-israel-1948.summary: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel. War with neighboring Arab states follows.

h-iranian-revolution.summary: A revolution overthrows the Pahlavi monarchy. Iran becomes an Islamic republic.

h-sokoto-caliphate.summary: Usman dan Fodio founds a caliphate in what is now northern Nigeria. It becomes West Africa's most populous state.

h-liberia-1847.summary: Settlers in a colony founded for freed Black Americans declare Liberia independent.

h-suez-canal.summary: A canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Ships no longer need to sail around Africa.

h-adwa.summary: Emperor Menelik II's army defeats an Italian invasion. Ethiopia keeps its independence.

h-year-of-africa.summary: Seventeen African nations win independence in a single year. Nigeria is the most populous of them.

h-south-africa-1994.summary: Citizens of all races vote for the first time. Apartheid ends, and Nelson Mandela becomes president.

h-rwandan-genocide.summary: Extremists carry out a genocide against the Tutsi during Rwanda's civil war.

h-indian-rebellion-1857.summary: Soldiers and civilians rise against the East India Company. Britain then takes direct rule of India.

h-partition-of-india.summary: British rule ends and India and Pakistan become independent. Partition uproots millions of people.

h-bangladesh-1971.summary: After a war of liberation, East Pakistan becomes the independent nation of Bangladesh.

h-first-opium-war.summary: Britain goes to war with Qing China over the opium trade. China cedes Hong Kong.

h-meiji-restoration.summary: Power returns to Japan's emperor. Japan modernizes rapidly.

h-xinhai-revolution.summary: An uprising at Wuchang brings down the Qing dynasty. China becomes a republic.

h-hiroshima-nagasaki.summary: The United States drops two atomic bombs on Japanese cities. Japan surrenders weeks later.

h-prc-1949.summary: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic in Tiananmen Square.

h-korean-war.summary: North and South Korea fight a war that draws in the United Nations and China. It ends in an armistice.

h-covid-19.summary: A new coronavirus spreads from Wuhan across the world in early 2020. The WHO ends the global emergency in May 2023.

h-indonesia-1945.summary: Sukarno reads the proclamation of independence. A war against Dutch rule follows.

h-fall-of-saigon.summary: North Vietnam captures Saigon. The Vietnam War ends.

h-indian-ocean-tsunami.summary: A huge earthquake off Sumatra sends tsunamis across the Indian Ocean.

h-tashkent-1865.summary: Russian forces attack Tashkent during their conquest of Central Asia.

h-sputnik.summary: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite. The space age begins.

h-louisiana-purchase.summary: The United States buys the vast Louisiana territory from France.

h-mexican-independence.summary: A long struggle ends Spanish rule in Mexico.

h-ayacucho.summary: Patriot forces defeat the last large Spanish army in South America.

h-american-civil-war.summary: The Union and the Confederacy fight over slavery and secession. The Union wins, and slavery ends.

h-transcontinental-railroad.summary: A golden spike joins the rails across the United States at Promontory Summit.

h-lei-aurea.summary: Princess Isabel signs the Golden Law, ending slavery in Brazil.

h-panama-canal.summary: A canal across Panama links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

h-wall-street-crash.summary: Stock prices collapse in New York. The worldwide Great Depression follows.

h-united-nations.summary: Delegates from around the world sign the charter that founds the United Nations.

h-apollo-11.summary: American astronauts become the first people to walk on the Moon.

h-september-11.summary: Al-Qaeda hijackers crash airliners in New York and near Washington. Nearly 3,000 people die.

h-treaty-of-waitangi.summary: The British Crown and Māori chiefs sign a treaty. New Zealand becomes a British colony.

h-nz-womens-suffrage.summary: A new law gives New Zealand women the vote. They vote in a general election that November.

h-australia-federation.summary: Six British colonies unite as the Commonwealth of Australia.
